relationships.rationale: Fairness, scoring, and overload semantics extend the scheduler-pass stages but are not the same lifecycle contract.
The same-wake cascade uses readiness transitions whose pending or reopened states conflict with the declared closed lifecycle.
Wake coalescing behavior interacts with the explicit runtime wake ordering and timeout constants without being synonymous with them.
Role capability ambiguity interacts with the single-scheduler boundary, while overseer role contracts remain distinct from scheduler authority.
Scheduler pass atomicity and readiness-input consistency share snapshot concerns but govern different scopes and failure surfaces.
Capacity reservation semantics interact with fairness and overload behavior, but capacity accounting and score policy remain distinct.
Known-good refresh behavior extends the Free Models catalog while retaining a distinct refresh lifecycle and recovery promise.
Override and unavailable-state visibility is consumed by the catalog but has a distinct user-visible state promise.
Wake and attempt mapping specializes the event-driven scheduler but retains its own transition contract.
Sound event taxonomy selects sound mappings and assets, while event classification and asset lifecycle remain distinct authorities.
A notification test delivery requires a destination configuration, but external test-send settlement is not a configuration mutation lifecycle.
Delivery and credential recovery produce outcomes consumed by receipt persistence, while transport recovery and durable storage remain separate.
Project attention and concern propagation consumes the shared alert lifecycle but also includes broader propagation and notification behavior.
Durable attention records persist and coalesce alert state, while mutation authority and storage lifecycle remain distinct.
Notification trust copy projects attention state and actions without becoming the canonical concern-resolution lifecycle.
